{
  "name": "builder_margin_topk_pairs_001",
  "intuition": "Pairs each candidate with clearly better ones (objective margin), then caps total pairs via top-k margin selection to stay within a pairing budget while emphasizing high-confidence preferences.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, N]
    B, N = objective.shape

    # Configurable thresholds/caps
    gap_thr = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 128))
    max_pairs_per_instance = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 64))

    # Build all better-than relations with an optional margin threshold
    # mask[b,i,j] == True means i is better (lower) than j by at least gap_thr
    diff = objective[:, :, None] - objective[:, None, :]  # [B, N, N]
    mask = diff < (-gap_thr)

    # Flatten pairs and compute margins (larger margin => higher confidence)
    b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx = mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    margins = (objective[b_idx, loser_idx] - objective[b_idx, winner_idx])  # [P]

    P = margins.numel()
    if P == 0:
        return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'margin_topk_pairs', 'gap_threshold': gap_thr, 'max_pairs': max_pairs, 'max_pairs_per_instance': max_pairs_per_instance})

    # Global cap
    k_global = max_pairs
    if k_global > P:
        k_global = P

    # Optional per-instance cap: keep at most max_pairs_per_instance pairs per batch item
    # Implemented by selecting top-k per instance using a dense [B, P] score matrix.
    # This avoids Python loops over pairs.
    if max_pairs_per_instance > 0:
        score = margins
        # Dense matrix of scores per instance; fill non-members with -inf
        score_mat = objective.new_full((B, P), float('-inf'))
        score_mat[b_idx, objective.new_zeros((P,), dtype=b_idx.dtype)] = float('-inf')
        arange_p = objective.new_zeros((P,), dtype=b_idx.dtype)
        arange_p = arange_p + objective.new_tensor(list(range(P)), dtype=b_idx.dtype)
        score_mat[b_idx, arange_p] = score

        k_pi = max_pairs_per_instance
        if k_pi > P:
            k_pi = P

        top_vals, top_idx = score_mat.topk(k=k_pi, dim=1)
        keep_pi = top_vals.reshape(-1) > float('-inf')
        sel_pi = top_idx.reshape(-1)[keep_pi]

        # Apply per-instance selection
        b_idx = b_idx[sel_pi]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[sel_pi]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[sel_pi]
        margins = margins[sel_pi]
        P = margins.numel()
        if P == 0:
            return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'margin_topk_pairs', 'gap_threshold': gap_thr, 'max_pairs': max_pairs, 'max_pairs_per_instance': max_pairs_per_instance})

        if k_global > P:
            k_global = P

    # Global top-k by margin
    top_m, top_i = margins.topk(k=k_global, dim=0)
    b_idx = b_idx[top_i]
    winner_idx = winner_idx[top_i]
    loser_idx = loser_idx[top_i]

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'margin_topk_pairs', 'gap_threshold': gap_thr, 'max_pairs': max_pairs, 'max_pairs_per_instance': max_pairs_per_instance})
"
}

{
  "name": "anchored_topk_pairs_001",
  "intuition": "Construct stable preferences by anchoring each instance’s best objective (winner) against a small top-k set of worse candidates, ensuring low-noise comparisons and explicit pair-budget control without randomness.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    B, N = objective.shape

    # Anchor each batch element on its best (lowest) objective completion.
    winner_idx = objective.argmin(dim=1)  # [B]

    # Rank candidates by objective (ascending); take a small set of worst-than-winner.
    order = objective.argsort(dim=1)  # [B, N]

    # Place winner first; choose losers from later ranks.
    k = int(extra.get('k_per_instance', 2))
    k = max(1, min(k, max(1, N - 1)))
    loser_rank = torch.arange(1, 1 + k, device=objective.device)
    loser_idx = order[:, loser_rank]  # [B, k]

    # Filter out ties: only keep if winner is strictly better (lower) than loser.
    w_obj = objective.gather(1, winner_idx[:, None])  # [B, 1]
    l_obj = objective.gather(1, loser_idx)  # [B, k]
    valid = (w_obj < l_obj)  # [B, k]

    b_idx = torch.arange(B, device=objective.device)[:, None].expand(B, k)
    w_idx = winner_idx[:, None].expand(B, k)

    b_idx = b_idx[valid]
    w_idx = w_idx[valid]
    l_idx = loser_idx[valid]

    # Optional global cap (deterministic): keep first max_pairs pairs.
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 128))
    if b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        b_idx = b_idx[:max_pairs]
        w_idx = w_idx[:max_pairs]
        l_idx = l_idx[:max_pairs]

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, w_idx, l_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'anchored_topk_pairs', 'k_per_instance': k, 'max_pairs': max_pairs})
"
}

{
  "name": "builder_gap_topk_pairs_002",
  "intuition": "Construct preferences from strictly better (lower) objective pairs but cap per-instance pairs via top-k smallest objective gaps to stay within a pairing budget while focusing on informative near-miss comparisons.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, K]
    B, K = objective.shape

    # Configurable caps/thresholds
    max_pairs_per_instance = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 128))
    gap_threshold = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))

    # Candidate pairs: winner has strictly lower objective than loser
    win_obj = objective[:, :, None]  # [B, K, 1]
    lose_obj = objective[:, None, :]  # [B, 1, K]
    gap = lose_obj - win_obj  # positive when winner is better
    mask = gap > gap_threshold  # strict + optional margin

    # Keep only top-k smallest gaps (hardest comparisons) per (B, winner)
    # Non-candidates get +inf so they are excluded from topk.
    inf = gap.max().detach() + 1.0
    gap_masked = gap.masked_fill(~mask, inf)  # [B, K, K]

    k = max(1, min(K, max_pairs_per_instance))
    vals, idx = gap_masked.topk(k=k, dim=-1, largest=False)  # [B, K, k]
    keep = vals < inf

    # Build pair indices without Python loops over pairs
    b_grid = objective.new_zeros((B, K, k), dtype=idx.dtype)
    w_grid = objective.new_zeros((B, K, k), dtype=idx.dtype)
    b_grid = b_grid + objective.new_tensor(range(B), dtype=idx.dtype)[:, None, None]
    w_grid = w_grid + objective.new_tensor(range(K), dtype=idx.dtype)[None, :, None]

    b_idx, winner_idx, sel = keep.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    loser_idx = idx[b_idx, winner_idx, sel]

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'gap_topk_pairs', 'max_pairs_per_instance': max_pairs_per_instance, 'gap_threshold': gap_threshold})
"
}

{
  "name": "builder_rank_stratified_cap",
  "intuition": "Build preferences by rank strata per instance (best vs near-best, mid vs mid+delta, and near-worst vs worst), giving broad coverage without exploding all-pairs; this keeps deterministic objective-based ordering but changes the mechanism from exhaustive comparisons to rank-based stratified pairing with a per-instance cap.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    B, K = objective.shape
    device = objective.device

    # Rank candidates per instance (lower objective is better).
    order = objective.argsort(dim=1, stable=True)  # [B, K]

    # Per-instance cap on number of pairs, while ensuring coverage.
    max_pairs_per_instance = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 2))
    max_pairs_per_instance = max(1, max_pairs_per_instance)

    # Deterministic offsets for pairing within each stratum.
    delta_near = int(extra.get('delta_near', 1))
    delta_mid = int(extra.get('delta_mid', 2))
    delta_tail = int(extra.get('delta_tail', 1))
    delta_near = max(1, delta_near)
    delta_mid = max(1, delta_mid)
    delta_tail = max(1, delta_tail)

    # Choose anchor ranks for strata; clamp for small K.
    r_best = 0
    r_mid = K // 2
    r_tail = max(0, K - 1 - (K // 4))
    r_worst = K - 1

    # Build candidate pair sets (winner_rank < loser_rank always).
    # Pair set 0: best vs near-best
    w0 = order[:, r_best]
    l0 = order[:, min(K - 1, r_best + delta_near)]

    # Pair set 1: mid vs mid+delta
    w1 = order[:, min(K - 1, r_mid)]
    l1 = order[:, min(K - 1, r_mid + delta_mid)]

    # Pair set 2: near-worst beats worst? Actually lower is better, so near-worst should beat worst.
    w2 = order[:, max(0, r_worst - delta_tail)]
    l2 = order[:, r_worst]

    # Stack pairs as [B, 3, 2] then select up to max_pairs_per_instance.
    winners = torch.stack([w0, w1, w2], dim=1)
    losers = torch.stack([l0, l1, l2], dim=1)

    # Filter invalid/self pairs (can happen when K is very small or deltas clamp).
    valid = winners != losers  # [B, 3]

    # Keep first N valid pairs per instance without Python loops.
    keep_n = min(3, max_pairs_per_instance)
    # Assign a large rank to invalid so they sort to the end.
    sort_key = (~valid).to(torch.int64)  # 0 for valid, 1 for invalid
    _, perm = sort_key.sort(dim=1, stable=True)  # valid-first
    perm = perm[:, :keep_n]  # [B, keep_n]

    wb = winners.gather(1, perm)
    lb = losers.gather(1, perm)
    vb = valid.gather(1, perm)

    # Flatten only valid pairs.
    b_idx = torch.arange(B, device=device)[:, None].expand(B, keep_n)
    b_idx = b_idx.reshape(-1)
    winner_idx = wb.reshape(-1)
    loser_idx = lb.reshape(-1)
    vflat = vb.reshape(-1)

    if vflat.any():
        b_idx = b_idx[vflat]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[vflat]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[vflat]
    else:
        # Fallback: ensure at least one pair if possible.
        if K >= 2:
            b_idx = torch.arange(B, device=device)
            winner_idx = order[:, 0]
            loser_idx = order[:, 1]
        else:
            b_idx = torch.empty((0,), device=device, dtype=torch.long)
            winner_idx = torch.empty((0,), device=device, dtype=torch.long)
            loser_idx = torch.empty((0,), device=device, dtype=torch.long)

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx),
        weight=None,
        meta={
            'builder': 'rank_stratified_cap',
            'max_pairs_per_instance': max_pairs_per_instance,
            'delta_near': delta_near,
            'delta_mid': delta_mid,
            'delta_tail': delta_tail
        }
    )
"
}

{
  "name": "builder_margin_topk_001",
  "intuition": "Construct pairwise preferences only when the objective gap is meaningfully positive (margin filtering) and cap the number of pairs per instance via top-k by gap to respect a pairing budget while prioritizing the most informative (largest-gap) comparisons.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # Lower objective is better.
    thr = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))
    max_pairs_per_instance = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 128))

    # gap[b,i,j] > 0 means i is better (lower) than j; filter by margin.
    gap = objective[:, None, :] - objective[:, :, None]
    valid = gap > thr

    # Score by gap; invalidate non-eligible pairs.
    score = gap.masked_fill(~valid, float('-inf'))

    # Select up to K pairs per instance by largest gap.
    K = max_pairs_per_instance
    if K <= 0:
        empty = objective.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)
        return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(empty, empty, empty), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'margin_topk', 'gap_threshold': thr, 'max_pairs_per_instance': K})

    topv, topi = score.view(score.shape[0], -1).topk(k=min(K, score.shape[1] * score.shape[2]), dim=1)
    picked = topv.isfinite()

    b_idx, flat_idx = picked.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    flat_pairs = topi[b_idx, flat_idx]
    N = objective.shape[1]
    winner_idx = flat_pairs // N
    loser_idx = flat_pairs % N

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'margin_topk', 'gap_threshold': thr, 'max_pairs_per_instance': K})
"
}

{
  "name": "anchored_topk_pairs_001",
  "intuition": "Pick a small, stable set of preferences by anchoring each instance on the best (lowest objective) candidate and pairing it against the worst candidates plus a few near-ties, yielding informative comparisons while respecting a strict global pair budget without randomness.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, N], lower is better
    B, N = objective.shape

    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 128))
    # Per-instance budget (at least 1) and capped by available opponents.
    per_inst = max(1, min(int(extra.get('pairs_per_instance', max(1, max_pairs // max(B, 1)))), max(N - 1, 1)))

    # Anchor on best (min objective).
    anchor = objective.argmin(dim=1)  # [B]

    # Exclude anchor by setting its score to +inf for selecting opponents.
    idx = torch.arange(N, device=objective.device).view(1, N)
    is_anchor = idx.eq(anchor.view(B, 1))

    # Opponents: mix of worst (largest objective) and near-ties (closest objective to anchor).
    obj_excl = objective.masked_fill(is_anchor, float('inf'))
    worst = torch.topk(obj_excl, k=per_inst, dim=1, largest=True, sorted=False).indices  # [B, per_inst]

    anchor_obj = objective.gather(1, anchor.view(B, 1))  # [B, 1]
    gap = (objective - anchor_obj).abs().masked_fill(is_anchor, float('inf'))
    near = torch.topk(gap, k=per_inst, dim=1, largest=False, sorted=False).indices  # [B, per_inst]

    opponents = torch.cat([worst, near], dim=1)  # [B, 2*per_inst]
    # De-duplicate while keeping order: unique via sorting by index; then take first K after stable mask.
    # Build a one-hot presence matrix for indices and re-extract up to per_inst unique.
    one_hot = torch.zeros((B, N), device=objective.device, dtype=torch.bool)
    one_hot.scatter_(1, opponents, True)
    one_hot.scatter_(1, anchor.view(B, 1), False)

    # Extract candidate indices per row in ascending order, then take first per_inst.
    cand_idx = one_hot.to(torch.int64).cumsum(dim=1)
    # Positions where cumsum in [1..per_inst] and one_hot is True
    take_mask = one_hot & (cand_idx <= per_inst)
    b_mat, j_mat = take_mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)  # flattened

    # Ensure we have exactly one winner (anchor) vs opponent (loser if higher objective, else swapped).
    a_flat = anchor[b_mat]
    o_flat = j_mat

    obj_a = objective[b_mat, a_flat]
    obj_o = objective[b_mat, o_flat]
    a_better = obj_a <= obj_o
    winner_idx = torch.where(a_better, a_flat, o_flat)
    loser_idx = torch.where(a_better, o_flat, a_flat)

    # Global downselect deterministically if over budget (keep smallest objective gaps).
    if b_mat.numel() > max_pairs:
        gap_sel = (objective[b_mat, loser_idx] - objective[b_mat, winner_idx]).abs()
        keep = torch.topk(gap_sel, k=max_pairs, largest=False, sorted=False).indices
        b_mat = b_mat[keep]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[keep]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[keep]

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_mat, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'anchored_topk_pairs', 'max_pairs': max_pairs, 'pairs_per_instance': per_inst})
"
}

{
  "name": "builder_stratified_rank_pairs_000",
  "intuition": "All parents reliably create objective-consistent (winner has lower objective) pairwise preferences, but they either explode to all pairs or use randomness/global caps that can miss instance coverage. This builder keeps the monotonic objective preference signal while switching to a deterministic, rank-based stratified scheme (near-best, mid, tail) with a per-instance cap to ensure broad coverage under a fixed budget.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, N], lower is better
    B, N = objective.shape

    # Per-instance cap and total budget (deterministic; no randomness).
    per_instance_cap = int(extra.get('per_instance_cap', 8))
    per_instance_cap = max(1, min(per_instance_cap, max(1, N - 1)))
    budget = int(extra.get('max_pairs', extra.get('pairing_budget', 128)))
    budget = max(1, budget)

    # Rank candidates within each instance (stable, deterministic).
    # order: indices sorted by objective ascending.
    order = objective.argsort(dim=1)

    # Stratified anchor ranks: best, mid, tail.
    r_best = torch.zeros((B,), device=objective.device, dtype=order.dtype)
    r_mid = torch.full((B,), N // 2, device=objective.device, dtype=order.dtype)
    r_tail = torch.full((B,), max(0, N - 1), device=objective.device, dtype=order.dtype)

    # Candidate loser ranks (exclude self): choose from opposite side to create informative gaps.
    # For best anchor: pair with top-K worst.
    # For tail anchor: pair with top-K best.
    # For mid anchor: pair with K/2 best and K/2 worst.
    K = per_instance_cap
    K_mid_lo = K // 2
    K_mid_hi = K - K_mid_lo

    # Build loser rank sets deterministically using slicing (no Python loops over pairs).
    # Note: if N==1, handled by per_instance_cap clamp above.
    worst_ranks = torch.arange(max(0, N - K), N, device=objective.device, dtype=order.dtype)  # [<=K]
    best_ranks = torch.arange(0, min(K, N), device=objective.device, dtype=order.dtype)       # [<=K]

    mid_best_ranks = torch.arange(0, min(K_mid_lo, N), device=objective.device, dtype=order.dtype)
    mid_worst_ranks = torch.arange(max(0, N - K_mid_hi), N, device=objective.device, dtype=order.dtype)

    # Expand anchors and loser ranks to [B, M] then map through order -> candidate indices.
    def _pair(anchor_r, loser_ranks):
        # anchor_r: [B], loser_ranks: [L]
        a_idx = order.gather(1, anchor_r[:, None]).expand(B, loser_ranks.numel())  # [B, L]
        l_r = loser_ranks[None, :].expand(B, loser_ranks.numel())
        b_l_idx = order.gather(1, l_r)  # [B, L]
        return a_idx, b_l_idx

    a_best, l_from_worst = _pair(r_best, worst_ranks)
    a_tail, l_from_best = _pair(r_tail, best_ranks)

    # Mid anchor: concatenate best-side and worst-side targets.
    a_mid1, l_mid1 = _pair(r_mid, mid_best_ranks)
    a_mid2, l_mid2 = _pair(r_mid, mid_worst_ranks)
    a_mid = torch.cat([a_mid1, a_mid2], dim=1)
    l_mid = torch.cat([l_mid1, l_mid2], dim=1)

    # Combine all candidate pairs: [B, P]
    anchor = torch.cat([a_best, a_mid, a_tail], dim=1)
    other = torch.cat([l_from_worst, l_mid, l_from_best], dim=1)

    # Remove self-pairs and ensure winner has lower objective.
    # We interpret (anchor, other) as an unordered candidate; pick winner/loser by objective.
    self_mask = anchor != other
    obj_a = objective.gather(1, anchor)
    obj_o = objective.gather(1, other)

    # winner is lower objective; drop ties.
    win_is_a = obj_a < obj_o
    win_is_o = obj_o < obj_a
    valid = self_mask & (win_is_a | win_is_o)

    winner = torch.where(win_is_a, anchor, other)
    loser = torch.where(win_is_a, other, anchor)

    # Flatten valid pairs.
    b_idx = torch.arange(B, device=objective.device, dtype=order.dtype)[:, None].expand_as(winner)
    b_idx = b_idx[valid]
    winner_idx = winner[valid]
    loser_idx = loser[valid]

    # Enforce global budget deterministically by taking a prefix (keeps instance coverage bias via construction).
    if b_idx.numel() > budget:
        b_idx = b_idx[:budget]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[:budget]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[:budget]

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'stratified_rank_pairs', 'per_instance_cap': per_instance_cap, 'max_pairs': budget})
"
}

{
  "name": "builder_rank_stratified_cap",
  "intuition": "Build preferences by rank-stratified matchups within each instance (best-vs-mid, mid-vs-tail, best-vs-tail), using ranks (not raw objective gaps) to stay robust to scale; cap pairs per instance with top-k to ensure coverage while controlling budget.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    B, N = objective.shape

    # Lower objective is better: sort ascending and operate in rank space.
    sorted_obj, sorted_idx = objective.sort(dim=1, descending=False)

    # Define three strata in sorted (rank) order: head, mid, tail.
    head_k = int(extra.get('head_k', max(1, N // 4)))
    tail_k = int(extra.get('tail_k', max(1, N // 4)))
    head_k = max(1, min(head_k, N))
    tail_k = max(1, min(tail_k, N))
    mid_start = head_k
    mid_end = N - tail_k
    mid_len = max(0, mid_end - mid_start)

    # Slice indices for each stratum.
    head = sorted_idx[:, :head_k]
    tail = sorted_idx[:, N - tail_k:]
    if mid_len > 0:
        mid = sorted_idx[:, mid_start:mid_end]
    else:
        # Fallback: use head as mid when no middle exists (very small N).
        mid = head
        mid_len = head_k

    # Per-instance cap; keep it small and deterministic.
    max_pairs_per_instance = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 8))
    max_pairs_per_instance = max(1, max_pairs_per_instance)

    # Build a fixed set of candidate pairs per instance using vectorized cartesian products.
    # 1) head vs tail (hard negatives)
    w_ht = head[:, :, None].expand(B, head_k, tail_k)
    l_ht = tail[:, None, :].expand(B, head_k, tail_k)
    # 2) head vs mid (near-best calibration)
    w_hm = head[:, :, None].expand(B, head_k, mid_len)
    l_hm = mid[:, None, :].expand(B, head_k, mid_len)
    # 3) mid vs tail (shape the tail)
    w_mt = mid[:, :, None].expand(B, mid_len, tail_k)
    l_mt = tail[:, None, :].expand(B, mid_len, tail_k)

    winners = torch.cat([
        w_ht.reshape(B, -1),
        w_hm.reshape(B, -1),
        w_mt.reshape(B, -1),
    ], dim=1)
    losers = torch.cat([
        l_ht.reshape(B, -1),
        l_hm.reshape(B, -1),
        l_mt.reshape(B, -1),
    ], dim=1)

    # Remove self-pairs (can happen with fallback mid=head).
    valid = winners != losers

    # Score pairs by rank distance to prioritize informative comparisons.
    # rank_pos[b, idx] = rank (0 best).
    rank_pos = torch.empty((B, N), device=objective.device, dtype=torch.long)
    rank_pos.scatter_(1, sorted_idx, torch.arange(N, device=objective.device, dtype=torch.long).view(1, N).expand(B, N))
    dist = (rank_pos.gather(1, losers) - rank_pos.gather(1, winners)).clamp_min(0)

    # Make invalid pairs unattractive for topk.
    very_neg = torch.full_like(dist, -10**9)
    score = torch.where(valid, dist, very_neg)

    # Select up to max_pairs_per_instance per instance.
    K = min(max_pairs_per_instance, score.shape[1])
    topk_score, topk_idx = score.topk(K, dim=1, largest=True, sorted=False)
    picked_valid = topk_score > -10**8

    b_idx = torch.arange(B, device=objective.device).view(B, 1).expand(B, K)[picked_valid]
    w_idx = winners.gather(1, topk_idx)[picked_valid]
    l_idx = losers.gather(1, topk_idx)[picked_valid]

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx, w_idx, l_idx),
        weight=None,
        meta={
            'builder': 'rank_stratified_cap',
            'head_k': head_k,
            'tail_k': tail_k,
            'max_pairs_per_instance': max_pairs_per_instance,
        },
    )
"

{
  "name": "builder_rank_stratified_cap",
  "intuition": "Build preferences by ranking candidates within each instance (lower objective is better) and pairing across strata (best-vs-mid and mid-vs-tail) with a per-instance cap, preserving full instance coverage while avoiding O(K^2) all-pairs expansion.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    B, K = objective.shape

    # Rank within each instance; lower objective => better rank.
    order = objective.argsort(dim=1, descending=False)

    # Stratify indices by rank: top, middle, bottom.
    top_n = int(extra.get('top_n', 2))
    mid_n = int(extra.get('mid_n', 2))
    tail_n = int(extra.get('tail_n', 2))
    top_n = max(1, min(top_n, K))
    mid_n = max(1, min(mid_n, K))
    tail_n = max(1, min(tail_n, K))

    top = order[:, :top_n]
    mid_start = max(0, (K - mid_n) // 2)
    mid = order[:, mid_start:mid_start + mid_n]
    tail = order[:, K - tail_n:]

    # Cross products within each instance (vectorized, no Python loops over pairs).
    # Winners are better-ranked groups (top/mid) against worse-ranked groups (mid/tail).
    w1 = top[:, :, None].expand(B, top_n, mid_n).reshape(B, -1)
    l1 = mid[:, None, :].expand(B, top_n, mid_n).reshape(B, -1)

    w2 = mid[:, :, None].expand(B, mid_n, tail_n).reshape(B, -1)
    l2 = tail[:, None, :].expand(B, mid_n, tail_n).reshape(B, -1)

    winner = torch.cat([w1, w2], dim=1)
    loser = torch.cat([l1, l2], dim=1)

    # Drop any accidental self-pairs.
    valid = winner != loser

    # Per-instance cap via slicing (keeps coverage across instances).
    max_pairs_per_instance = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 8))
    max_pairs_per_instance = max(1, max_pairs_per_instance)

    # Compact valid pairs to the left using sort-by-mask trick.
    # This avoids Python loops while enabling deterministic truncation.
    sort_key = (~valid).to(torch.int64)  # valid -> 0, invalid -> 1
    perm = sort_key.argsort(dim=1, stable=True)
    winner = winner.gather(1, perm)
    loser = loser.gather(1, perm)
    valid = valid.gather(1, perm)

    keep = min(max_pairs_per_instance, winner.shape[1])
    winner = winner[:, :keep]
    loser = loser[:, :keep]
    valid = valid[:, :keep]

    b_idx = torch.arange(B, device=objective.device)[:, None].expand(B, keep)

    b_idx = b_idx[valid]
    winner_idx = winner[valid]
    loser_idx = loser[valid]

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx),
        weight=None,
        meta={
            'builder': 'rank_stratified_cap',
            'top_n': top_n,
            'mid_n': mid_n,
            'tail_n': tail_n,
            'max_pairs_per_instance': max_pairs_per_instance,
            'mid_start': mid_start
        }
    )
"
}

{
  "name": "builder_anchor_topk_margin",
  "intuition": "Build stable, budgeted preferences by comparing each candidate to per-instance best and worst anchors, plus a small set of hardest (small-margin) objective-improving pairs to focus learning on informative distinctions without exploding pair count.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    B, N = objective.shape

    # Budget controls
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 128))
    k_hard = int(extra.get('k_hard', 2))
    k_hard = int(max(0, min(k_hard, max(0, N - 1))))

    device = objective.device

    # Anchors: best (min objective) and worst (max objective) per instance
    best_idx = objective.argmin(dim=1)  # [B]
    worst_idx = objective.argmax(dim=1)  # [B]

    arange_b = torch.arange(B, device=device)

    # Pair everyone against best anchor when best is strictly better
    obj_best = objective[arange_b, best_idx]  # [B]
    mask_best = obj_best[:, None] < objective  # [B, N]
    mask_best[arange_b, best_idx] = False
    b1, l1 = mask_best.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    w1 = best_idx[b1]

    # Pair worst anchor against everyone it is strictly worse than
    obj_worst = objective[arange_b, worst_idx]  # [B]
    mask_worst = objective < obj_worst[:, None]  # [B, N]
    mask_worst[arange_b, worst_idx] = False
    b2, w2 = mask_worst.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    l2 = worst_idx[b2]

    # Hard pairs: per winner, pick up to k_hard closest worse losers (smallest positive margin)
    # margin[w,l] = objective[l] - objective[w]
    obj_w = objective[:, :, None]
    obj_l = objective[:, None, :]
    margin = obj_l - obj_w  # [B, N, N]
    valid = margin > 0

    if k_hard > 0 and N > 1:
        inf = torch.tensor(float('inf'), device=device, dtype=objective.dtype)
        margin_pos = torch.where(valid, margin, inf)
        _, topk_loser = torch.topk(margin_pos, k=k_hard, dim=2, largest=False)  # [B, N, k]
        b3 = torch.arange(B, device=device)[:, None, None].expand(B, N, k_hard).reshape(-1)
        w3 = torch.arange(N, device=device)[None, :, None].expand(B, N, k_hard).reshape(-1)
        l3 = topk_loser.reshape(-1)
        # Filter out non-valid selections (inf margins)
        m3 = (margin[b3, w3, l3] > 0)
        b3 = b3[m3]
        w3 = w3[m3]
        l3 = l3[m3]
    else:
        b3 = torch.empty((0,), device=device, dtype=torch.long)
        w3 = torch.empty((0,), device=device, dtype=torch.long)
        l3 = torch.empty((0,), device=device, dtype=torch.long)

    # Combine all pairs
    b_idx = torch.cat([b1, b2, b3], dim=0)
    winner_idx = torch.cat([w1, w2, w3], dim=0)
    loser_idx = torch.cat([l1, l2, l3], dim=0)

    # Deterministic capping: keep pairs with smallest objective margin (hardest) up to max_pairs
    if b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        d = (objective[b_idx, loser_idx] - objective[b_idx, winner_idx]).to(dtype=torch.float32)
        k = int(max_pairs)
        _, sel = torch.topk(d, k=k, largest=False)
        b_idx = b_idx[sel]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[sel]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[sel]

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'anchor_topk_margin', 'max_pairs': max_pairs, 'k_hard': k_hard})
"
}

{
  "name": "builder_sampled_pairs_gapweight_001",
  "intuition": "Sampled pairwise preferences can be noisy when objective gaps are tiny; filtering by a configurable minimum gap and weighting by (clipped) gap emphasizes clearer wins and improves generalization.",
  "implementation_hint": {
    "expects": [
      "objective",
      "log_prob"
    ],
    "returns": "PrefBatch",
    "mode": "pairwise"
  },
  "code": "def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    mask = objective[:, :, None] < objective[:, None, :]
    b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx = mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)

    # Optional gap thresholding to reduce ambiguous preferences
    gap_threshold = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))
    if b_idx.numel() > 0 and gap_threshold > 0.0:
        gap = (objective[b_idx, loser_idx] - objective[b_idx, winner_idx])
        keep = gap >= gap_threshold
        b_idx = b_idx[keep]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[keep]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[keep]

    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 123))
    if b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        # Deterministic subsample: keep the largest-gap pairs
        gap = (objective[b_idx, loser_idx] - objective[b_idx, winner_idx])
        topk = torch.topk(gap, k=max_pairs, largest=True, sorted=False).indices
        b_idx = b_idx[topk]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[topk]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[topk]

    weight = None
    if b_idx.numel() > 0 and bool(extra.get('use_gap_weight', True)):
        gap = (objective[b_idx, loser_idx] - objective[b_idx, winner_idx])
        w_cap = float(extra.get('gap_weight_cap', 10.0))
        weight = gap.clamp(min=0.0, max=w_cap)

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=weight, meta={'builder': 'sampled_pairs_gapweight', 'max_pairs': max_pairs, 'gap_threshold': gap_threshold, 'use_gap_weight': bool(extra.get('use_gap_weight', True))})
"
